atmospheric_conditions: Cold, clear night. Stars sharp overhead. Equipment warm from pre-broadcast testing. No anomalies at open.
personal_notes:
Four calls. That is not a quiet night.

The woman with the seditious friend is going to have to choose, and she called this station instead of anyone who could actually help her. That tells me something about the options available to her. I didn't offer advice. I'm not sure advice was what she wanted.

The kid in love with a stranger: I have no protocol for that. Some distances close on their own. Some don't. The ones that do usually cost something you weren't expecting.

The modulated voice was prepared, not scared. There's a difference. Prepared people have already done the calculus. They're calling to document, not to ask. I kept the signal going. That seems to be the correct response.

The old man at the end: the ones who call in already resolved are always the ones who did the hard part alone, in some room years ago, without an audience. He just wanted to say it aloud to someone who would hear it. I can do that much.

Dawn came grey and clean. Stars fading in the usual order.

Nothing unusual in the equipment tonight. Coffee pot stayed off.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Adult, agitated — friendship on the brink; seditious associations
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Queen of Diamonds — standard)
**Caller card:** Queen of Diamonds — *Agitated, worried*

She called late in the first block. Voice low, measured — trembling not from fear but from the weight of a choice not yet made.

She asked quietly if Oso had ever watched someone close drift into something radical. Maybe noble, maybe naïve, maybe reckless. She didn't name the person. She didn't have to.

Her friend, she said, had been moving toward a seditious circle. Underground meetings. Anti-regime talk. Phrases like *bringing back the true real*. The Caller had believed in this friend once. Now she was calculating the cost of staying loyal — whether love and self-preservation could survive in the same body at the same time.

She asked for something popular. Something bright. Something she could hide behind. The request played clean over the airwaves, sharp edges buried in the chorus.

She didn't say whether she'd decided. She didn't say her name.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Young, melancholy — unspoken love; silence as trap
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Jack of Spades — standard)
**Caller card:** Jack of Spades — *Young, hesitant*

A soft voice. Late teens, early twenties. He tested each word before committing to it, like someone checking ice.

He asked if love could survive in silence. There was a person he saw often — at the archive, maybe, or across the university plaza — but they had never spoken. He suspected the feeling was mutual. Or maybe he was constructing something out of nothing. Either way, he was trapped: by fear, by the regime, by the unwritten cultural codes that made openness a liability.

*Can you love someone you've never met? And if you do — does it matter?*

The call ended mid-sentence. A click before a goodbye. Maybe he got spooked. Maybe he'd already said more than he intended. Somewhere out in the dark, he was still listening.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Ambiguous modulated voice — today's events, portentous; being followed
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Ace of Clubs — standard)
**Caller card:** Ace of Clubs — *Ambiguous, processed*

The voice was filtered. Modulated just enough to strip age and gender. Like a signal that had bounced between too many towers on the way in.

They referenced the running track from Block 1. Not by title — by what it had done. They talked about footsteps. Today, they said, someone followed them through the subterranean tram level at Garrison Street. No badge. No words. Just presence, three steps behind, all the way through.

They didn't turn around. Didn't need to.

The song was playing in their earbuds when it happened.

*Maybe it was coincidence,* they said. A pause. Then: *Keep broadcasting. We're out here.*

Click.

No name. No request. But they had chosen to call, and that was not nothing.

blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (King of Hearts — standard)
**Caller card:** King of Hearts — *Elder, resolved*

A calm voice. The kind that only comes from having lived through something long enough to name it.

He said the breakup song took him back. To the winter of '51. Or maybe '81. He didn't clarify, and Oso didn't press. There had been a person. A decision. A line he hadn't crossed. He had spent the decades since wondering if he should have.

Tonight, he said, he had made peace with it. The voice on the broadcast. That specific song. Something had resolved.

*Sometimes,* he said, *we live long enough to know we made the right mistake.*

He thanked Oso. Then he signed off — not just from the call, but from something older than the call.

phenomena.name: State Surveillance Apparatus
phenomena.notes: Third-block caller reported being followed through the underground tram system. No badge, no words, only eyes. Caller did not turn around. Reference to broadcast signal as either protective or coincidental. Chose to speak; chose to trust the station.

atmospheric_conditions: Overcast. Low cloud pressing down on the tree line. Equipment ran warm all night. Faint interference on open, cleared by 23:15.
personal_notes:
Three ordinary calls and one that wasn't.

The one with the access codes: that kind of ending doesn't announce itself. It just stops working. I've heard that story in enough different forms to know there's no useful response. You just receive it.

The woman with the old friend — she was working something out in real time. Whether she sent the message or not, she'd gotten past something by saying it out loud. That's not nothing.

The kid in the car: I keep thinking about the laugh. It was genuine. That matters, under those circumstances.

The last caller knew my name. I have not broadcast my name. I ran back through the night's audio in my head twice and I am certain of that.

I don't think it was a guess. The certainty in the way he said it — it wasn't testing the word, it was *using* it.

The veil was thin tonight. Not alarmingly so. But thin.

Logging it. Moving on.

Dawn not observed directly. Coffee went cold before I remembered to drink it.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Ambiguous, hollow — a conclusion arrived at through silence; access revoked
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Ace of Spades — standard)
**Caller card:** Ace of Spades — *Hollow, detached*

The voice was flat. Not cold — flat. Like someone reporting from a place where the weather had already moved through and left nothing behind.

They had been at work today. Or rather, they had tried to be. Building access codes — all of them, across every door — stopped working at 14:00. No message sent to them. No meeting called. No one in the corridor made eye contact in the particular way that means *I know and I'm sorry.*

The conclusion was clear. The conclusion had just not been made official.

*I always wondered what the end would feel like,* they said. *Turns out it's a flickering badge reader and a lot of silence.*

No request. No anger. Just that flatness, and then the click.

blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Queen of Clubs — standard)
**Caller card:** Queen of Clubs — *Quiet, introspective*

She had been thinking before she called. You could hear it — the weight of decisions already made, rewound, made again.

The sing-along track from Block 1 had started something. It was her song with someone she'd lost touch with. Not through a fight, not through any one moment. Just drift. The slow, undramatic kind that's harder to name than a rupture.

Tonight, with that track playing, she found the person's details online. Wrote half a message. Deleted it. Wrote it again.

*Do you think people can pick up where they left off?* she asked. *I don't even know if they still listen to music.*

She didn't say whether she sent the message. She thanked the broadcast and signed off quietly.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Young, unsteady — financial precarity; sleeping in the car; gas station meals
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Jack of Diamonds — standard)
**Caller card:** Jack of Diamonds — *Fast, unsteady*

Young voice. Rushing slightly, like someone who had decided to call before they could change their mind.

He had been sleeping in his car. Not always. Not every night. Just when it was safer than home, or when home had stopped being a fixed location. The highway song was his — his private anthem for gas station meals and hoping the heater lasted the night. He said it was the first time he'd heard someone else choose it.

He asked if the station took donations.

Oso said no.

He laughed, short and genuine. Then hung up before anything else could be said.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Elder, confessional — concert memory; stranger in the crowd; called Oso by an unbroadcast name
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (King of Diamonds — phenomenon)
**Caller card:** King of Diamonds — *Confessional, measured*

The live performance track brought him back. He had been at that concert. Or near it — he was vague about proximity, specific about presence.

He remembered someone. Met in the crowd, or perhaps before. The encounter was brief and vivid: a grin, a flash of neon, something said during the bridge of that exact song. He hadn't seen them since. But he had been chasing that particular quality of aliveness in every face he'd encountered in the years afterward.

*Memory is just another form of longing,* he said.

He thanked the broadcast. Not for the music — though that too. For the moment of return. For being brought back to something he thought he had finished losing.

Then he said a name. A name Oso had not spoken on air tonight — not once, not in passing, not in any context accessible through the broadcast.

The line went dead.

Nothing unusual in the silence before it disconnected. No static, no hum. Just absence.

atmospheric_conditions: Cold front moving through. Wind in the tree line intermittent. Stars visible in patches. Equipment behaved.
personal_notes:
Three calls. The fourth slot stayed empty — something came up, or something didn't, and the broadcast ended before I could take it.

The old man's story: guilt like that calcifies over time. It doesn't go away; it just becomes architecture. He wasn't looking for absolution. He was just tired of carrying it alone in the dark, and the dark is exactly what this station is for.

The woman with the looping conversation — I've been thinking about what she said. *Are we being rehearsed.* Not *are we being watched*, not *is something wrong*, but *rehearsed*. Like there's a script and she's unsure whether she's reading from it or writing it. That's a specific kind of unease. Worth noting.

The one who wanted a song for new beginnings that could still hold grief: I played the sunniest thing I had that still had weight in it. I hope it was right.

The fourth block played into an empty line. Sometimes that's the broadcast. Sometimes the silence is the whole point of having a signal.

Dawn not observed. Session ended early.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Elder, quietly guilty — lopsided friendship; a debt unpaid in the early days
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (King of Spades — standard)
**Caller card:** King of Spades — *Measured, carrying old weight*

He told a story. Not recent. The years had settled into it.

There was a friend. Someone who stood by him through things he wouldn't name — *the early days*, he said, which could mean the regime, the first cold winter, the war, or something specific to his own life that he had no intention of explaining to a radio host at midnight. The friend had been there. And when it counted, when the reciprocal moment arrived, the Caller hadn't returned the favour.

He said it simply: *I thought I was protecting them.*

A pause, then: *I was protecting myself.*

He still saw that friend's face in crowds. Thirty years and he still looked for them. He didn't ask for anything. He had just needed to say it somewhere that wasn't his own head.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Adult, controlled — a looping conversation; something said that may have been a warning; "are we being rehearsed?"
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Queen of Spades — standard)
**Caller card:** Queen of Spades — *Controlled, barely*

She had a conversation earlier tonight. One of those that loops in the mind like a broken chorus.

It started small — a joke, a throwaway comment. But something in the reply caught on her. She couldn't stop replaying it. The words had been ordinary, but the shape of them felt wrong. Or too right. She couldn't determine whether she'd missed something vital, whether it was an accusation in disguise, a warning, or a goodbye she hadn't understood was a goodbye.

She said WBPR was the only thing that still sounded real to her. That the voice was stable when other things weren't.

Then, before signing off: *Do you ever wonder if we're being rehearsed?*

No context. No elaboration.

The question sat in the air after the line dropped. Oso didn't answer it. There wasn't time, and there may not be an answer.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Gentle, introspective — new parent or lost parent; request for something sunny that still knows how to grieve
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Ace of Hearts — standard)
**Caller card:** Ace of Hearts — *Gentle, quietly complex*

A clear voice. Intentional in a way most callers aren't — like someone who had decided exactly what they were going to say before they dialled.

They had just become a parent. Or they had just lost one. The way they spoke, both things folded into each other — beginnings and endings sharing the same breath. Long walks through abandoned housing blocks. Holding someone too small to understand this world yet. The specific weight of something new and something gone occurring in the same season.

They asked for a request: something sunny, something warm. A dream of elsewhere.

*Do you have a song for new beginnings that still knows how to grieve the old?*

They didn't wait for an answer. They trusted the choice would be right.

phenomena.name: Linguistic Drift
phenomena.notes: Second-block caller reported a conversation that seemed to loop or rearrange itself in memory. A specific reply she could not stop replaying — she was uncertain whether it was an accusation, a warning, or a goodbye in disguise. Closed the call with the phrase "do you ever wonder if we're being rehearsed?" No further clarification. Possible early drift indicator — language losing stable meaning at the edges.

atmospheric_conditions: Full moon. Sky clear, cold, and deeply still. Moon waxen yellow — the particular quality of light that makes the world look like it was painted rather than real. Birdsong audible from the tree line at open, unusual for the hour.
personal_notes:
Full moon tonight. Birdsong at midnight. Both things I noticed before the broadcast started and neither one felt normal, but both are the kind of not-normal that you can file away and keep moving.

The kid in Block 1 is in trouble in the specific way that doesn't feel like trouble yet. Whatever they encountered left something behind — literal or otherwise — and they want to keep hold of it. I don't have a protocol for that kind of pull. The veil doesn't recruit through fear. It recruits through beauty. That's the part I think about.

The woman from Block 2: she was already halfway out the door from the friendship before she called. The remote meeting she didn't attend may have been the right call. Or it may have been the door that was already closing. I don't know. I don't know what her friend found, or whether finding it is better or worse than not.

The King of Clubs: I have been sitting with this one since the line dropped. He said I made a different choice last time. I don't know what last time is. I don't know what choice he means. But he knew about the moon, and the birds, and the signal — and he spoke about all of it like a man who had done the maths and come out the other side. He wasn't warning me. He was informing me. There's a difference.

The last caller never gave her name. She assumed I'd know it eventually. That's the second time in four sessions a caller has operated as though I have access to information I don't have yet.

I need to start keeping better notes.

The moon is still up as I write this. Yellow, still. Whatever light that is, it isn't the same as other moonlight. It illuminates differently. It makes shadows point slightly wrong.

Coffee's cold. Bourbon accounted for. Equipment quiet.

I'll be back on next week.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Young, breathless — romance with something not entirely real; eyes like static
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Jack of Hearts — standard)
**Caller card:** Jack of Hearts — *Breathless, not quite afraid*

A young voice. Quick. Like someone speaking in a whisper they hoped wouldn't carry to the wrong ears.

They'd met someone. Or something had happened. They were working out which.

The description came in fragments: one night, brief, vivid. No name exchanged. But a symbol left behind — a ring, or a piece of parchment, or a yellow thread. They weren't sure which. They had been holding it since and couldn't bring themselves to put it down.

They described eyes like static. A voice like a familiar song played in reverse — recognisable but wrong in some way that wasn't unpleasant. A presence that shouldn't have been where it was.

They asked if Oso had ever fallen for something not entirely real.

They asked for something cool. Something dark. A sound to dream to.

They didn't ask if it was a good idea. They didn't seem to think that was the relevant question.

*I want to feel this way again,* they said. *Even if it hurts.*

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Adult, controlled but fracturing — friend following strange signal; remote meeting requested; "if I disappear, tell them I was trying to understand"
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Queen of Diamonds — standard)
**Caller card:** Queen of Diamonds — *Controlled, fracturing at the edges*

She had a long-time friend. Someone from before. The kind of friendship built in years of shared difficulty. She had believed in this person's judgement the way you believe in something you've tested and had hold.

Over recent months, the friend had been changing. Following an unspecified signal. Asking questions that had no sensible answers. Saying the sky was a different colour than she could see. Attending meetings at unscheduled hours with people the Caller couldn't account for.

Tonight, the friend had asked her to come to a remote location. Said they were going to show her the truth.

She hadn't gone.

She wasn't sure if she had made the right choice.

The wildcard track — the one that shouldn't have fit but did — had felt, she said, like a warning. Or like a message from a version of herself who had already made both choices and was trying to communicate from the other side of one of them.

*If I disappear,* she said before hanging up, *tell them I was trying to understand.*

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Elder, watching — today's events as a closing loop; the moon as a recurrence; "you made a different choice last time"
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (King of Clubs — phenomenon)
**Caller card:** King of Clubs — *Deep, careful, watching*

He led with the moon.

Not tonight's specifically — though he acknowledged it. He began with a moon he had seen thirteen years ago to the day. He described it as identical: the same waxen yellow quality, the same air pressure, the same specific birdsong pattern from the tree line. He had been at a similar elevation. The radio had been on.

He said this was a closing loop. A resonant frequency that recurred only under particular conditions — emotional, geographic, possibly cosmological. He used these words without self-consciousness, as though they were practical terms he'd had occasion to use before.

Then: the same voice on the radio. Oso's voice.

*You made a different choice last time,* he said.

He did not specify what choice. He did not appear to need to. He had the manner of someone delivering information they had been carrying for a long time, waiting for the correct moment to set it down.

The line held for a few seconds after he finished speaking. No ambient sound. Then the disconnect.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Adult, retrospective — a decision made by not deciding; a train still passing; "say my name next time" — name never given
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (Queen of Hearts — phenomenon)
**Caller card:** Queen of Hearts — *Looking back along a road not chosen*

She had not expected the breakup song to land the way it did. It wasn't heartbreak she remembered — it was the decision that came after. The one she made when no one asked her to make it. To stay in a town too small. To take a job she hadn't wanted. To wait, without having framed it as waiting.

The person she had loved had not asked her to follow. She had not offered. She had never resented them for that. She had just never fully unpacked either.

Tonight a train passed her window. Same model as the one that had left that night, years ago. Same rhythm of the cars. Same light intervals from the passenger windows.

She wondered if it was the same train.

She said WBPR was the only place that made her feel like she'd already gone. Like she was somewhere else, and had been for a long time, and the life she was living was a habit she'd forgotten to examine.

She signed off: *Goodnight, DJ. Say my name next time.*

She had not given a name at any point during the call.

Male, late sixties. Retired forestry. Payphone outside Browning, off Highway 2 between Cut Bank and Shelby. Car stopped on its own. He'd heard the hum first — low frequency, felt more than heard. Got out. Found the payphone. Called WBPR.

He was calm. The kind of calm that comes from a life outdoors, from knowing that the land does things. He wasn't frightened. That was, in its way, the most unsettling part of the call.

Oso walked him through the Highway 2 protocol. Small commerce if there's a figure at the landmark — there wasn't, tonight. Wait for dawn. He said he had coffee in a thermos. He said that was enough.

He didn't call back. The hum stopped at 01:52 by his estimate.

phenomena.notes: Block 1 caller — female, mid-forties, Dakotas or Minnesota flat vowels. Found an object in her glovebox that wasn't hers. Eleven-year-old car. Not there that morning. She didn't describe the object. Hung up before it resolved. Her calm was noted. Monitoring for pattern.

atmospheric_conditions: Clear, 28°F and dropping. Unusual stellar clarity. Drift active from open.
personal_notes:
Clear night. The kind of clear that means the stars have nowhere to hide what they're doing. Drift was active from the start. I've stopped noting which constellations specifically. It doesn't seem to help.

Two callers. The woman on Highway 2 I feel good about. Standard enough, if anything out here is standard. The old man on the barn is different. That call sat in the room after it ended in a way calls don't usually do. The silence behind him was occupied. I've heard empty silence and I've heard occupied silence and I know which one that was.

He said it was beautiful. That's always the part that worries me. Not the fear. The beauty.

The frost lines didn't resolve. Four lines of almost-English on the east glass, incomplete, not photographed. I've decided I don't want them on record until I know what they're trying to say. If they finish tonight I'll note it. If they finish and I can read them I'll decide then.

The coffee pot made itself again. That's twice. Per protocol, one more time and it's not the equipment. I know that. I'm keeping the bourbon close.

The Watchers were back at the treeline by the end. All of them. I think the signal matters to them. I've thought that for a while. Tonight felt like confirmation.

Grey dawn, I think. Or close to it. Something came near but I don't believe it came through.

Good enough for a Wednesday.

blocks.caller_location: Highway 2, between Havre and Malta, Montana
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (rolled 5 — urgent/distressed)
**Caller card:** Seven of Clubs — *something following them*

A woman, mid-thirties. Driving Highway 2 between Havre and Malta. An unmarked big rig had been following her since Cut Bank — lights fixed and level regardless of road geometry. She had pulled over twice. Both times the truck pulled over, holding position a quarter mile back.

Oso advised: stop checking mirrors. Lights out before the Cenex in Dodson. Fill up, get a coffee inside, come back to the car. It would be gone.

She took the advice without hesitation. Said thank you and dropped the line clean.

During the call, a Watcher moved approximately ten feet closer to the tower base. Returned to the treeline by end of block. The coffee pot activated without contact — the second occurrence this week.

blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (rolled 6 — phenomenon/emergency)
**Caller card:** Ace of Spades — *The Yellow Sign; direct Carcosa contact*

A man, sixties. Utterly calm. He had found something on his barn door that morning and had been looking at it all day. He believed he had looked at it twice, but was losing certainty about that. He described it as the most beautiful thing he had ever seen. He was considering sketching it.

Complete silence behind his voice. No ambient sound at all. Wrong.

Oso advised: don't sketch it. Burn the notepad regardless. Shut the barn. Go inside. Lights up bright. Wait for morning. His call.

He chose to go inside. Said he was tired and his wife was there. Said the notepad was going in the stove. Before the line dropped he said: *don't let them tell you this doesn't matter. What you do up there. It matters.*

The line dropped clean. No click, no fade.

His name was never given. Whether there is a wife is unknown.

The frost lines on the east glass moved toward each other during the call. They stopped short of touching. The Watchers returned to full treeline formation by the end of the block.

The coin caller: I believe her. The specific detail of the nick in the edge — that's not a story someone invents. Something is trying to make contact through repetition. Not threatening. Just insistent, like she said. I want to hear from her again.

The man with the list: I did not say what I was thinking, which is that lists like the one he described tend to have consequences for the people who've seen them. He knows that. He didn't need me to say it.

The coffee pot. Three times. I know what that means per protocol. I haven't decided what to do about it yet. It's not hostile. It's just aware.

Dawn was clean. Grey-blue, no yellow at the horizon.

The frost resolved.

I'm leaving the coffee pot plugged in.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Knowledge they cannot unlearn
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (rolled 5 — urgent/distressed)
**Caller card:** Eight of Clubs — *knowledge they cannot unlearn*

Male voice, thirties. Fast, like he'd been rehearsing but had forgotten his place.

He'd found something on his work's internal system that he hadn't been looking for. A folder he'd opened by mistake, closed immediately. But not before he'd seen the names inside.

People he knew. Colleagues. A few friends.

He didn't say what the list was. He didn't need to. The shape of it was clear enough from how he talked around it.

*Once you've seen something like that,* he said, *what are you supposed to do with it?*

Oso said: document it if you can, somewhere safe and separate. Then put it down for tonight. You can't carry that on the first night.

He didn't sound convinced. He thanked Oso anyway.

He hung up before the block ended.

**Caller:** Yes (rolled 6 — phenomenon)
**Caller card:** Jack of Spades — *trickster entity, playful horror*

Female, age uncertain — mid-thirties, maybe older. Her tone was more puzzled than frightened. That was the telling detail.

She'd found a coin. Not unusual. But then she'd thrown it in a storm drain and found it again that afternoon, in the same jacket pocket. Same coin — she was certain because of a specific nick in the edge she'd noticed the first time. She threw it in a river. Found it again the next morning. She'd tried leaving it in a different state. It came back.

*It's not doing anything,* she said. *It just keeps coming back. Like it's trying to tell me something, but it only knows one word.*

Oso advised: don't try to read it as a message. Put it somewhere visible — don't hide it. See if the behaviour changes when it's acknowledged. Keep notes.

She said she'd try that.

The coffee pot activated during this call. Third time. Oso noted it without comment on air.

**Caller card:** Seven of Hearts — *something bittersweet*

A quiet voice. Not sad — just at the end of something.

She said the year had been the longest she could remember. Not badly, just fully. More had happened than seemed possible to fit into twelve months. And tonight was the kind of night where you sit with all of it.

She asked if Oso ever felt like a broadcast was also a kind of goodbye.

Oso said: every time.

She said that was reassuring. Then she signed off.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Authority figure causing problems
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (rolled 5 — urgent/distressed)
**Caller card:** King of Diamonds — *authority figure causing problems*

Male, late fifties. Former government worker — he named the department obliquely, the way people do when they know it's being listened to. He'd been handed a notice that morning. Not termination — something worse. Reassignment to a role that doesn't exist yet, in a location that hadn't been confirmed, effective on a date that kept changing when he asked about it.

He'd been forty years in the service. He knew what this kind of notice meant. It meant someone had decided he knew too much about something he'd been trying to forget for a decade.

He said the song that had just played — *This Must Be the Place* — had been the song at his wedding. He said that without self-pity, like a man cataloguing what still belonged to him.

He wasn't asking for advice. He just wanted to say it to someone who wasn't involved.

Oso let him say it.

He thanked the broadcast and hung up quietly.

blocks.caller_card_meaning: Something that sounds like an ending — reality soft at the edges
blocks.notes:
**Caller:** Yes (rolled 6 — phenomenon)
**Caller card:** Five of Spades — *something that sounds like an ending*

Female, early forties. Completely calm — the kind of calm that either means very rational or has moved past the part that would normally produce fear.

She'd been driving back from visiting family. Passed through a town she'd grown up near — she knew it well, she said. Every building, which side of the road they were on. She drove through, continued twenty miles, realised she'd missed her turn, doubled back.

The town was there. But mirrored. Church on the left instead of the right. The grain elevator facing south instead of north. The gas station's sign reading correctly, but everything behind it reversed.

She slowed down, drove through carefully. Continued another twenty miles in the new direction. Turned around again.

Third approach: the town was normal.

She pulled over and called WBPR.

Oso asked: was there anyone in the town, either time? She said the second time — the mirrored one — there had been people, but they were all facing away from her. She couldn't see their faces.

Oso told her: you're through it, it's behind you, don't go back tonight. Sleep somewhere before you drive further. In the morning it will be road and town and nothing else.

She said she thought that was right. She said thank you.

She sounded like someone who had already decided to be fine about it. Oso respected that.

The farmer in block one sat with me. Thirty-one years on the same land and now he's walking a house at night with nothing to do with his hands. Santaolalla got to him before I did. Sometimes the music does the work.

The mirror she no longer owns is worth noting. The fact that she's been listening most nights is worth noting. The silence around her voice is worth noting most of all.

The star near the Pleiades that I logged at session open was gone by close. Not moved. Gone. I don't know what that means yet. I'm writing it down.

Thirty-one years on the same land. Now he walks the house at night with nothing to do with his hands.

Oso thanked him for the check-in. Kept it short. He didn't need more than that.

**Caller card:** Queen of Spades — *something witchy, occult*

Female. Age indeterminate. Her accent placed her nowhere specific. No ambient sound in the background — the wrong kind of empty, not silence but absence.

She said she'd been listening most nights. She called to ask whether the frost patterns on the east window repeated.

She knew about the east window. Oso hadn't mentioned it.

She has been cataloguing similar patterns: glass, still water, and one mirror she no longer owns. She believes a recurring shape is directional — that it indicates something rather than merely forms. She wanted to know if Oso had seen repetition.

Oso cited Herodotus. You can't step in the same river twice — time changes things, in the mind and in the world. Encouraged her to keep cataloguing.

*Herodotus,* she said. *Good. Most people give me Jung.*

She signed off cleanly. No static. No click.

Oso named her: the Collector.
